title: Top Aviation Firms
h1: Not revealed by search snippets. Search-result title of the case-study page is "Top Aviation Firms". A separate non-case-study page https://www.silveroakcapital.co.uk/top-aviation-firms/ carries the title "Top Aviation Finance Law Firms in London".
summary: Case study of an aircraft-finance enquiry routed to Silver Oak Capital through an aviation finance law firm. Deal as revealed: a law firm's private client team asked Silver Oak Capital to source financing for its client's purchase of a Bombardier G6000 business jet. Borrower: an Egyptian national (private individual, introduced by a law firm). Structure requested: an operating lease agreement, for flights between Cairo, Dubai and London. Amount: the client wanted to finance 80% of a $35 million purchase price (i.e. roughly $28m, 80% LTV; the $28m figure is arithmetic, not stated). Asset: Bombardier G6000 business jet, over 8 years old. Lender type: European lenders are referenced as the market (most would place the client in a high-risk category). Challenge: (1) the client's Egyptian nationality placed him in the high-risk category for most European lenders; (2) a high loan-to-value was challenging for an aircraft over 8 years old. Timing: not revealed. Outcome: NOT revealed by the search results (neither the lender found, the terms, nor whether the deal completed). Framing: the page sits within Silver Oak Capital's claim that it 'has partnered with some of the top aviation finance law firms in the world' so clients get 'complete and independent advice when arranging aircraft loans'. Related aviation case studies surfaced alongside: Gulfstream G650 ($40m, 80% LTV, 10-year term, European private bank) and Falcon 900 (70% LTV, 4.45% fixed, 72-month term, Dubai-based client).

notes: Direct fetch blocked; everything comes from two extended WebSearch calls (tagged [a] = exact-URL query, [b] = site: keyword query). Items marked 'tool paraphrase' are the search tool's own summary wording, not page text. The $35m x 80% = $28m figure is arithmetic, not stated. The slug 'top-aviation-firms' exists twice on the site: this case study and a top-level page /top-aviation-firms/ titled 'Top Aviation Finance Law Firms in London', which also circulates as a SlideServe/SharePresentation deck; tool [a] warned that some of those related pages 'read as promotional and contain garbled text' and that the firm's self-described standing is unverified marketing. Two site URLs not in the seed were surfaced: /top-aviation-firms/ and /aviation-finance-lease-advisory/. Unrelated results (DigitalDefynd, FasterCapital) ignored.
